summary: No new blocking defect found at this exact head. Both first-review findings are substantively fixed and independently verified with bounded executable probes. This is a code-review disposition, not a declaration that outstanding native-image, style, platform or performance gates passed.

resolved_prior_findings.evidence: The exact head expression utf8.length < MAX_STACK_STRING_BYTES - stackStringsUsed was extracted into a Java probe and matched long arithmetic for 1,526,850 cases. All used values 0..256 were tested with lengths 0..1024 and MAX_VALUE-1024..MAX_VALUE, plus one million seeded random pairs. Prior (used=16,length=2147483639) case is rejected. Accepted transitions keep used in 0..256; this invariant makes the subtraction and subsequent increment safe. No giant arrays were allocated.

NFITest.lookupAndBindDefault maps strcmp to reexport_strcmp on Windows. Exact candidate string.c compiled as a Windows PE x86-64 object using MinGW with -Wall -Wextra -Werror, and the real .drectve section contains the reexport_strcmp export. Signature and strcmp forwarding match the test. Windows execution was not performed.

verified: Read canonical root, substratevm and truffle AGENTS.md plus suite READMEs; inspected the complete seven-file base-to-head diff before reading prior-review rationale. No nested instructions exist in the changed modules.

Exact baseline/head javaStringToUtf8 methods and the baseline ZeroTerminatedCharSequence class were extracted via git show. 77,763 bounded cases matched logical terminated output, including every UTF-16 code unit, 2,197 adversarial triples, 10,000 seeded random strings and ASCII/multibyte/surrogate-pair boundaries. Replacement bytes are therefore preserved on this host JDK; baseline excess buffer capacity was deliberately not treated as semantic output.

The fixed string boundary tests now include 254/255/256/257 ASCII bytes and multibyte boundaries. Two equal 127-byte arguments exactly fill the 256-byte arena including terminators; 128/255/256-byte pairs cover mixed/fallback behavior.

UnsafeStackValue allocations lower with SubstrateTarget.stackAlignment through StackValueNode, so byte-sized allocation does not imply byte-only address alignment. Primitive type offsets retain existing alignUp logic. Raw heap pointer creation and copyForward execute inside the uninterruptible method, with layout computation done before converting the object address.

Inspected current ObjectLayout signature: getArrayBaseOffset takes element size, so Byte.BYTES correctly adapts the API. The imported UnmanagedMemoryUtil and UnsafeStackValue exist at the current guest.staging locations.

NFI docs guarantee string argument pointers only during the native call. Stack argument storage lives across ffiCall including callbacks, and native string return allocations still use the separate javaStringToUtf8/strdup path. Array patches still call refArray and preserve read/write semantics instead of copying guest array contents into the primitive stack buffer.

Patch processing and ffiCall remain inside cleanup, so exceptions there close primitive fallback views and free heap argument-pointer tables. Outer LocalNativeScope still closes pinned argument arrays/strings and local handles. Fallible view construction before cleanup and malloc multiplication concerns already exist at the baseline and are not new changes.
The exact new C sum fixtures compiled with -Wall -Wextra -Werror and returned 65535 and 131071 for the distinct-bit 16/17-argument cases through host ctypes/libffi.
git diff --check baseline..exact-head passed; candidate HEAD and clean worktree rechecked when writing this report.
test_gaps: The new 16/17-argument tests use 128/136 primitive bytes and do not directly cover the 256-byte primitive-copy boundary or >256-byte primitive-view fallback. A 32/33-sint64 fixture or equivalent would close this gap.
No new test forces GC inside a callback while multiple stack strings and primitive pointers are live. Source lifetime review found no defect, but focused stress would improve coverage.

The malformed-surrogate JUnit test checks only length and surrounding characters to allow backend differences; it does not itself enforce the SVM question-mark replacement. The independent extracted-method probe does test that behavior.

NFICallOverheadTest warms call targets but does not assert compilation. Its informational minimum timing is not proof of compiled execution or performance improvement, and fallback strings are not benchmarked.
observations: Large-string fallback encodes once for stack selection and then re-encodes/copies in scope.refString. This is an allocation/performance tradeoff requiring measurement for long strings and exhausted arenas; no fresh performance claim is made.
No public API or documented lifetime contract changes were found; the patch is scoped to native-image NFI marshaling plus relevant test fixtures.
